realtimeTransport.title: Real-time transports
realtimeTransport.diagramLabel: Sequence diagram of {mode} between client and server over {seconds} seconds

captions.idle: Press play, or step through the timeline.
captions.serverUpdate: Update #{update} is ready on the server.
captions.pollRequest: Client asks the server: anything new?
captions.emptyResponse: Nothing new. That round trip was wasted.
captions.dataResponse: Client receives update {updates}, {delay} ms after it was ready.
captions.handshake: Client opens a WebSocket with an HTTP upgrade request.
captions.handshakeAck: Connection open. The server can now push at any time.
captions.pushArrives: Client receives update #{update}, {delay} ms after it was ready.
captions.longPollRequest: Client asks for news. The server holds the request open until it has some.
captions.longPollData: Client receives update {updates}, {delay} ms after it was ready, and asks again right away.
captions.longPollTimeout: No news before the timeout. The server answers empty and the client asks again.
captions.sseRequest: Client opens an EventSource: a normal HTTP request whose response stays open.
captions.sseOpen: Stream open. The server can now send events down the response at any time.
captions.sseEvent: Server sends event #{update} down the open stream.
captions.sseEventArrives: Client receives event #{update}, {delay} ms after it was ready.
captions.ssePost: To send data, the client makes a separate HTTP request. The stream only goes one way.
captions.ssePostDone: The separate request completes. The stream stays open.
captions.clientMessage: Client sends a message on the same connection. No new request needed.
captions.clientMessageArrives: Server receives the message right away, on the connection it already has.

realtimeTransport.legendHeld: Request held open by the server

rendering.title: Rendering strategies
rendering.diagramLabel: Timeline of server, network and browser work during a page load with {mode}

screen.partial: Page with a placeholder for the slow part

captions.idle: Press play, or step through the page load.
captions.csrShell: The server sends an almost empty HTML shell.
captions.csrParse: The browser can only show a blank page or a spinner.
captions.csrBundle: The browser downloads the whole JavaScript bundle.
captions.csrExecute: The JavaScript runs and starts fetching data.
captions.csrData: The page waits for the API response.
captions.csrRender: React renders the page in the browser.
captions.csrInteractive: Content appears and works at the same time, but only after everything has loaded.
captions.ssrRender: The server fetches data and renders the full HTML.
captions.ssrHtml: Complete HTML travels to the browser.
captions.ssrPaint: The browser paints the content right away.
captions.ssrBundle: Content is on screen, but the JavaScript that makes it work is still downloading.
captions.ssrHydrate: React hydrates: it attaches event handlers to the HTML already on screen.
captions.ssgHtml: A CDN serves HTML that was built ahead of time, close to the user.
captions.ssgPaint: The browser paints the content almost immediately.
captions.ssgBundle: The JavaScript bundle downloads in the background.
captions.ssgInteractive: Interactive. With ISR, the CDN rebuilds the page in the background once it goes stale.
captions.streamShell: The server renders the fast parts and starts streaming right away.
captions.streamShellHtml: The shell streams to the browser while a slow query keeps running on the server.
captions.streamPaint: The browser paints the shell and fast content, with a placeholder for the slow part.
captions.streamBundle: Only client components ship JavaScript, so the bundle is small.
captions.streamInteractive: Interactive, even though the slow part is still loading.
captions.streamRest: The slow part streams in on the same response.
captions.streamRestPaint: The browser swaps the placeholder for the real content.

retries.title: Retry timing

explanation.immediate: No delay: clients immediately repeat the failed read together.
explanation.backoff: Exponential delays reduce frequency, but clients still retry together.
explanation.jitter: Full jitter spreads retries inside each backoff window. Fixed samples make this demo repeatable.

captions.idle: Three clients are about to make the same read.
captions.first: The first requests run together; all three will fail.
captions.retrying: Retry requests are in flight. Compare their alignment across clients.
captions.waiting: Clients wait before retrying instead of adding immediate load.
captions.recovered: All three clients have succeeded on their third attempt.

retries.legend: × failed attempt; ✓ success. Every bar is one request. Times and outcomes are illustrative.

race.title: Out-of-order search

captions.idle: Search responses can arrive in a different order from the requests.
captions.first: The user searches for r. Its request will be slow.
captions.second: The user now searches for react. The new request will finish first.
captions.newResult: Results for react arrive and match the current input.
captions.ignored: The older r response arrives but is ignored. Results still match react.
captions.stale: The older r response overwrites the newer results. The input still says react.

race.diagramLabel: Older search completes after the newer search
race.note: Both requests finish in both modes. The guard controls which response may update the screen.

rate.title: Debounce vs throttle

policy.debounce: Trailing debounce: emit the latest value after 300 ms without input.
policy.throttle: Leading-only throttle: emit immediately, then drop inputs for 300 ms.

captions.idle: The same seven numbered inputs are used in both modes.
captions.input: Inputs keep arriving. The selected policy decides when to dispatch.
captions.dispatch: A value is dispatched without waiting for the entire interaction to end.
captions.done: All eligible dispatches are complete. Compare their timing and retained values.

rate.diagram: Input events and dispatched values over time
rate.note: Numbers identify the input values. Illustrative times; no network requests are made.

captions.idle: Compare the same resources with different discovery order.
captions.html: The HTML response is arriving first.
captions.resources: Watch which requests can begin before earlier work finishes.
captions.ready: All resources needed for this example content are ready.

note.serial: Here JS discovers data, then data reveals the image URL. Times are illustrative.
note.parallel: Here data and the image URL are known from HTML, so work overlaps. Equal task durations are assumed; shared bandwidth can change real results.

virtualization.title: A thousand-row list

captions.idle: A fixed-height list has 1,000 items and a five-row viewport.
captions.full: Scrolling changes the visible rows, but all 1,000 rows remain mounted in the model.
captions.windowed: Only visible rows plus two overscan rows on each side are mounted in the model.
captions.end: The viewport has reached the last five items. Compare the modeled mounted-row count.

virtualization.diagram: Sketch of the current five-row viewport
virtualization.note: The sketch draws only visible rows in both modes. Counts model a real list; this is not a DOM benchmark.
